en.title: Fewest Classes Under a Skill Difference Limit
en.description:
Divide all students into classes so that any two students in the same class differ in skill by at most maxSpread; find the minimum number of classes. Groups do not need to keep original indices adjacent, and different students with the same skill must all be placed.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n maxSpread; the second line contains the skills. The original text gives n≤100000 and a skill upper bound of 10^9, but the lower bounds were damaged in typesetting and no bound was given for maxSpread; this site explicitly uses 1≤n≤100000, 1≤skill≤10^9, 0≤maxSpread≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 2 and 1. Adjacent skill differences all being ≤1 does not mean 1,2,3 can share a class.
hints: Sort the skills; each class starts from the smallest unassigned student and absorbs everyone whose skill is at most that skill plus maxSpread.
